title: Regular completed coefficients and the quotient Koszul fiber
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $T$. On $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$, with their projections and quotient transitions [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Use cochain derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. There are a unit $u\in O^\times$ and $e\geq1$ with $\ell=u\pi^e$; the two sequences of ideals are cofinal. The rings $O/\pi^j$ and $O/\ell^n$ are finite for all $j,n\geq1$. The canonical maps identify $R/\ell^nR=B_n$ and $R/\pi^jR=(O/\pi^j)_T$. Multiplication by every $\ell^m$ and $\pi^j$ is injective on $R$. The augmented two-term complexes $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^m}R]\to B_m$ and $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R]\to(O/\pi^j)_T$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, are finite free K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex].

For $n\geq m\geq1$ set $P_{n,m}=B_n\otimes_RK_m=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n]$, with augmentation $\epsilon_{n,m}:P_{n,m}\to B_m$ given by reduction in degree zero, and $F_{n,m}=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_{n,m})[-1]$. The map $B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ with degree $-1$ coordinate $x\mapsto\ell^{n-m}x$ in $P_{n,m}^{-1}$ (and zero other coordinates) is a quasi-isomorphism of $B_n$-complexes. In particular $H^{-1}(P_{n,m})=\ell^{n-m}B_n\cong B_m$ and $H^0(P_{n,m})=B_m$. For $n'\geq n\geq m$, the coefficient reduction $F_{n',m}\to F_{n,m}$ corresponds under these quasi-isomorphisms to multiplication by $\ell^{n'-n}$ on $B_m[1]$. These statements include $n=m$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-completed-coefficient-regular-quotients] to the given $\ell,E,O,\pi,T$. It gives the unit factorization, positive ramification exponent, cofinality, finite quotients, regularity on every site object, and the actual quotient identifications, with the specified coefficient projections and all transitions. These are exactly the coefficient hypotheses needed below.

proof.text: The tensor clause sp_ell_coefficient_tensor is proved directly. The constant scalar section ell is the natural-number section, since the sheafification unit and the map into the completion are ring homomorphisms. Consequently its multiplication map is ell times the identity, and its iterated composite is ell^(m+1) times the identity. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] to the actual total tensor with the principal Koszul cone. Both resulting tensor factors are the quotient single complex tensored with the degree-zero unit. The right unitor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies each with that quotient single complex. Additivity transports the differential to ell^(m+1) times its identity. The induced isomorphism of arrows gives the isomorphism of cones. No regularity or inequality m <= n is needed for this clause.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-regular-scalar-quotient-exact-row] on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $(R,t)=(\mathcal O_{E,T},\ell)$ and then with $t=\pi$. Step 1 verifies sectionwise regularity and identifies the quotients with the stated constant sheaves through their actual augmentations. Thus both $K_m$ and $L_j$ are the asserted finite free K-flat resolutions; the normalized quotient augmentation gives $\epsilon_{n,m}$ for the tensor model already identified above. Its exact row identifies $\ker(\ell^m)$ with $\ell^{n-m}B_n\cong B_m$, and its final cokernel is $B_m$. By the definition of cohomology these are $H^{-1}(P_{n,m})$ and $H^0(P_{n,m})$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-exact-row-augmentation-fiber] over $S=B_n$ to the exact row of step 2, taking $(A,B,C,D)=(B_m,B_n,B_n,B_m)$, $a=a_{n,m}$, $d=\ell^m$ and $q=\mathrm{red}$. It identifies the shifted cone with $[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n\xrightarrow{-\mathrm{red}}B_m]$ and makes the specified coordinate map $i_{n,m}:B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: First proof paragraph, coefficient tensor and power transitions; assembly of the three extracted arguments.

proof.text: For $n\prime\geq n\geq m$, regard both exact rows as $B_{n\prime}$-linear by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use $(\beta,\gamma,\delta)=(\mathrm{red},\mathrm{red},1)$ and $\alpha=\ell^{n\prime-n}$ on $B_m$. The middle and right squares commute with scalar multiplication and reduction. On a local lift $x\in R$, the left square is $\ell^{n\prime-m}x\bmod\ell^n=\ell^{n-m}(\ell^{n\prime-n}x)\bmod\ell^n$; local representatives suffice by step 1. Naturality in [lem-sp-exact-row-augmentation-fiber] now gives $r i_{n\prime,m}=i_{n,m}\ell^{n\prime-n}$ strictly. Inverting the quasi-isomorphisms gives the claimed transition. At $n=m$, $a=1$, $d=0$ and the last two terms are $B_m\xrightarrow{-1}B_m$; thus the same formulas include the boundary case.
